NOTE TO THE TEACHERS
This booklet is intended to be a help in preparing Sunday school les-
sons. The title, subject, and topics are only the menu. It is your respon-
sibility to prepare the meal.
The proper ingredients are the salty inspirations of the Holy Spirit,
seasoned with His grace. Bake the ingredients at a hot temperature in the
oven of prayer. The time-tested recipe for preparing a nutritious meal is
found in 2 Timothy 2:15, "Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a
workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of
truth."
LESSON 1
CHRIST IN CREATION
Scripture Texts: Genesis 1:1, 26; John 1:1-4; Colossians 1:16-17; He-
brews 1:1-3; Revelation 1:8
Today, we begin a series of lessons on the life of Christ. He is the be-
ginning and the end, the first and the last. He is that "which is, and which
was, and which is to come, the Almighty" (Revelation 1:8).
Although this study will be an attempt to cover the life of Christ, in
reality, it is only a small portion of His life. It is impossible to see anything
eternal in its entirety, and Christ's life is eternal. It always was and always
will continue. To make this more real to us, we are including more than
Jesus' life on earth. The life of man begins with his birth and ends with his
death—not so of Christ. He lived before His birth; He lives after His death.
Read Psalm 104 before personally studying this lesson.
MEMORY VERSE: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or
ever the earth was.
—Proverbs 8:23
Let Us Make Man
Genesis 1:1 The first act of Christ of which we know is Creation. In the
beginning God—before there was anything else, there was God. The un-
iverse had a beginning and will have an end. God was first before Creation
and must hold that place in all of His creation.
Man is a combination of human and divine, of the earthly and the heaven-
ly. We are all part of God; we are like Him; His stamp is upon us. This lays
a serious responsibility upon each of us every day to keep from marring that
image by sin and to confine ourselves within the holy purposes of God. God
created—the Creator is three Persons: God the Father, God the Son, and
God the Holy Spirit.
Genesis 1:26 Let us make man in our image, after our likeness—the
Creator here spoke of Himself in the plural. This proves Jesus Christ was
with the Father before the world was (John 17:5).
Christ Lived Before His Birth
John 1:1-3 In the beginning was the Word ... with God ... was God.
Here we see both the eternity (since He existed as long as God) and the deity
(Godhood, state of being God) of Jesus Christ. We can see that Jesus is the
One spoken of by reading verse 14. All things were made by him. Christ
was the Agent in Creation.
Scientists are continually trying (unsuccessfully) to discover the secret of
life. They have made flowers that look and smell like a living flower but have
never been able to put life into them. They have made many things that ap-
pear to be real, but they are artificial—no life in them. God alone holds life.
He gave life at Creation, and still He is the only One who can give it. Best
of all, He has the will to give it.
Colossians 1:16-17 Everything was created by Christ, not only material
things but those of mind and spirit also—visible and invisible ... thrones ...
dominions ... principalities ... powers. All the laws of physics and nature,
of right and wrong, thought and emotion, of powers and possibilities
wrapped up in a human being were set there by Jesus Christ. He is before
all things, and by him all things consist—Christ is greater than all His cre-
ation. He was here first. He has power over it all. He holds all things togeth-
er and moves them in their ordered courses; all things are subject under Him.
In John 8:56-58, Jesus made it clear by His own testimony that He was
here before Abraham. The Jews then, as many do today, refused to believe
Him.
Christ, the Revelation of God
Hebrews 1:1-3 Christ is the Son by whom God hath in these last days
spoken unto us by ... whom also he made the worlds; who being the
brightness of his glory—of the Father's glory—express image of his per-
son—the Father's person. The Son is one with the Father—upholding all
things by the word of his power. His Word is enough to control the uni-
verse, from the vastness of space to the smallest microscopic things.
Himself purged our sins—the lowly Jesus who died for us is now sitting
on the right hand of the Majesty on high—at the right hand of the Father.
Here is a beautiful picture of Christ's creatorship, deity, glory, power, saving
work, and rulership. Oh, praise God! Does this not move you to worship
Him? God speaks to us through this lovely One. Listen and hear Him.
The Voice
Revelation 1:8 I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end ...
is ... was ... is to come—the eternity, both past and future, of Jesus Christ
is stated here. Who is speaking? Jesus Himself, for the statement begins, "I
am ...." (Read Revelation 2:8; 21:6; Isaiah 48:12.) He knows and reveals
this truth to us. Also, He is the Almighty—the all-powerful One. He can do
anything and everything.
John 1:4 In him was life—God the Father gave "to the Son to have life
in himself" (John 5:26). Our life is granted to us by God. We have no power
over it. Christ must give us life, or we are left dead. Christ gives a more
abundant type of life—eternal life, as He and the Father have. It comes from
Christ the Creator and no other source. This life becomes light to men. With
this light comes knowledge of things that cannot be known, understanding
that cannot be understood, a vision of things that cannot be seen, hope in a
hopeless world, joy and love. Have you been re-created by the Creator? You
can be. Think about it.
JUST A THOUGHT
The standard is the Bible. Take every doctrine and
opinion back to it for measuring.
LESSON 2
ISAIAH'S VISION OF CHRIST
Scripture Text: Isaiah 6:1-10
We know little of Isaiah's history, but it is enough to know that he was a
prophet of God. Today we study just one of a number of prophecies that he
prophesied about Christ. He called his prophecy the vision of Isaiah ...
which he saw, meaning that it came from God to him and was not his own
thinking (Isaiah 1:1).
Jesus Christ visited the earth before He was born into it. Today we study
one such visit as told by Isaiah, who saw Him. This was in the Temple of
Jerusalem in the year that king Uzziah died—758 B.C. Uzziah died from
leprosy resulting from his rebellion against God. Jesus appearing on the earth
before His birth shows that He existed then. In his vision, Isaiah found that
in Christ was life.
MEMORY VERSE: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall
I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.
—Isaiah 6:8
Holy, Holy, Holy
Isaiah 6:1 I saw also the L ORD sitting upon a throne, high and lifted
up, and his train filled the temple. The Lord was Jesus Christ. The throne
was because He is "KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS" (Revela-
tion 19:16). He is the exalted One, the One "before all things" (Colossians
1:17), whose "name ... is above every name" (Philippians 2:9).
Isaiah 6:2 Above it—the throne on which the Lord was sitting—stood
the seraphims—a close relationship in which they had been placed by the
Lord—each one had six wings—God's ministering angels. They were honor-
ing and worshiping the Lord. There needs to be more honor and greater re-
spect and reverence in our worship to the Lord. With twain he covered his
face—he wanted to see nothing of his own, but to see through the eyes of the
Lord the things to be seen. With twain he covered his feet—he wanted to
walk no way except the way the Lord led. And with twain he did fly—in the
power by which one is able to rise above the fleshly desires and deeds of the
human and follow the Lord on a higher plane of living with the Spirit lead-
ing. (Read Ezekiel, Chapters 1-3.)
Isaiah 6:3 And one cried ... Holy, holy, holy, is the L ORD of hosts. If
the Lord is to be seen high and lifted up there must be seraphims to cry out.
Seraphims are a type of God's ministering servants, those who are holy and
preach holiness. The message here is Holy God, Holy Son, Holy Spirit. It is
holy all the way through. Nothing short of a message of holiness will fill the
temple of God. It is no wonder that those who do not believe in holiness or
living a holy life are dead, and their worship is lifeless. The whole earth is
full of his glory. There was so much glory in the Temple that the whole earth
was full of the glory of God. When the temple is filled, it causes these
earthen vessels to receive more of His glory than they can contain.
Isaiah 6:4 And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that
cried—the cry of Holy, holy, holy, from a Spirit-filled ministry will cause
the door to the way people live to become more narrow—the house was
filled with smoke—the presence of God. Only holy preaching will fill the
house with the presence of God (Psalm 72:19).
Holiness Condemns Sin
Isaiah 6:5 Isaiah, amazed, and overwhelmed, looked and listened. This
is Jesus Christ, the Lord. Isaiah sensed His holiness in a flood of new
revelation. It caused him to humble himself in a rush of conviction of his own
sin. Repentance overcoms him. The sight of goodness condemned sin as no
words can. A holy life is the greatest proof of holy living. When the unsaved
see Jesus active in our lives, it is the greatest evangelism we can have. Woe
is me! for I am undone ... I am a man of unclean lips ... for mine eyes
have seen the King, the L ORD of hosts. What a contrast! Isaiah, unclean,
dead in sin, did not fit into this glorious scene (Psalm 1:5). When we see
Jesus as He is, we see ourselves as we are.
Isaiah 6:6-7 Flew one of the seraphims—acting as Christ's agent—hav-
ing a live coal ... from off the altar. Coming from the altar where the sacri-
fice was offered, which was a type of Jesus' death on the Cross, the live coal
symbolized His cleansing blood. This hath touched thy lips; and thine ini-
quity is taken away, and thy sin purged. God always meets true repentance
with forgiveness and cleansing. Cleansing is only through the blood of
Christ.
The Natural Response
Isaiah 6:8 God's cleansing is just the beginning. Whom shall I send, and
who will go for us? Who are "us"? The Trinity (Father, Son, and Holy
Spirit). God has work to be done and seeks those willing to do it. As soon as
one is cleansed from sin, God calls to service. Here am I; send me—Isaiah
heard and gave himself. God does not force, but invites. He can use only
those who consecrate themselves to Him. True happiness is found only when
one yields himself wholly to the Lord.
Isaiah 6:9-10 God had need of a messenger—a prophet. Go, and tell this
people. The duty of each messenger today is to take Christ's message of
warning to a sinful people. Lest they see ... and hear ... and understand ...
and convert, and be healed. To see and hear and understand and obey the
message of holiness is the only way to be healed of sin. Christ is "not willing
that any should perish" (2 Peter 3:9). God gives us the result of our own
choice, the fruit of our sowing (Matthew 13:10-15; John 12:37-41). This is
a warning to us. It is possible to neglect God's call until our ears hear it no
more, our minds understand it no more, and we lose the salvation we once
could have had.
God's Plan
The vision of today's lesson came at the beginning of Isaiah's prophetic
work. He went on to record more prophecies concerning Christ and His king-
dom. It would not have been possible for him to write the great Book of
Isaiah without his surrender and cleansing. What God can do in our lives de-
pends upon our answer to Him when He calls. Ask yourself: "Is my life
filling the pattern God planned? Am I letting Him use me?" His design for
every life is good, but He can carry it out only with those who listen and
yield.
JUST A THOUGHT
You cannot walk with God and run with the devil.
LESSON 3
CHRIST APPEARED TO NEBUCHADNEZZAR
Scripture Text: Daniel 3
Again, Jesus visited the earth before His birth, this time to protect and
deliver His faithful children. It occurred about 600 B.C. in Babylon, where
the Jews were captives. Nebuchadnezzar was the most powerful of the Baby-
lonian kings. Babylon was the capital of Chaldea. Shadrach, Meshach, and
Abednego were captive Jews from Canaan whom the king had placed in
important positions in the province of Babylon.
MEMORY VERSE: Little children, keep yourselves from idols. Amen.
—1 John 5:21
The King's Idol
Daniel 3:1, 4-6 Nebuchadnezzar the king made an image. He knew
something about God from his contact with Daniel (Daniel 2:47), but he had
not left his idol worship. It is commanded—a king's command has great
authority. And whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall ... be cast
into the midst of a burning fiery furnace. A fearful threat, who could with-
stand it?
The Plot
Daniel 3:8-12 Accused ... Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego ... have
not regarded thee: they serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden
image. Three men against the greatest king in the world—how dared they
take such a stand? As has been said of another, they "feared man so little be-
cause they feared God so much." They had heard the king's command, but
they knew God's Law—"Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image ....
Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them" (Exodus 20:4-5). They obeyed
with no excuse or compromise—nothing to take off any of the pressure.
The Challenge
Daniel 3:13-18 Nebuchadnezzar in his rage and fury ... spake ... who
is that God that shall deliver you out of my hands? He was not challenging
the men, but God. God always accepts a challenge like that. The rage and
fury would have caused most men to compromise, but not these men. They
had their backs against the wall, but they stood firm with their God. We are
not careful—this took courage of a higher order than man can muster on his
own. They had received their positions from this king, but their sights were
set on higher goals. They had received higher positions than those the king
had given them. Our God whom we serve is able to deliver .... But if not
... we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image. Their obedi-
ence did not depend on God's deliverance. They would be true, furnace or no
furnace, burned or not burned.
In the Furnace of Fire
Daniel 3:19-25 Heat the furnace one seven times more—a type of the
Gospel Day. We are living in a day heated by the fire of all seven ages.
These men were bound ... cast into ... the burning fiery furnace. No mer-
cy. Was this the point that all hope is gone, the time to give up? Many have
done so and lost the victory that was already theirs to take. Then Nebu-
chadnezzar looked. The king was astonied, and rose up in haste. Some-
thing had suddenly changed his attitude. Did not we cast three men bound
.... Lo, I see four men loose, walking ... no hurt; and the form of the
fourth is like the Son of God. It was a miracle. Jesus Christ Himself came
down to walk with His children in the fire. They had not known this would
happen; they had been faithful anyway.
The King Glorified God
Daniel 3:26-28 Come forth .... upon whose bodies the fire had no
power, nor was an hair of their head singed, neither were their coats
changed, nor the smell of fire had passed on them. Here we see God's
abundance (Ephesians 3:20). Jesus not only delivered, He walked with them
in the trial. He not only kept their bodies from being burned, but their clothes
from the smell of fire. Friend, He can save you and me from being tainted
by sin all around us. He can deliver from every sin. He can walk with us
through every circumstance man throws us into, and we can "live soberly ...
and godly, in this present world" (Titus 2:12).
Daniel 3:29-30 There is no other God that can deliver after this sort.
There is nothing so convincing as seeing the power of God in action. Having
seen it, the king was convinced.
Effective Faith
Sometimes we think we could trust more easily if we could just see with
our eyes proof of God's power. No, faith is not dependent upon natural sight
and sound. It is "the evidence of things not seen" (Hebrews 11:1). Nebuchad-
nezzar had much outward proof of God, yet was very slow to trust Him.
Read Daniel, Chapter 4, to see what it took to cause him to give up himself
and give praise to God. It is not enough to acknowledge God's existence and
power. We must take Him personally, as these Jewish men did, and separate
ourselves to Him. The memory verse gives this warning: "Keep yourselves
from idols." Keep clear and separate from all the many things set in the place
of God or between us and God.
Our danger may not be that of bowing before a golden image, but what
about loving something else more than God? "Covetousness ... is idolatry"
(Colossians 3:5). How about the temptation to trust in a picture, cross, or
some other object? God wants us to have close personal contact directly with
Him. Any object or form looked to as an aid to worship can become an idol
placed between ourselves and God. This will shut off the flow of His life into
ours. (Read Exodus 20:4-6.)
There is a great need for effective faith and courage. There is too much
weak-kneed compromise, destroying of the dividing lines between right and
wrong, and bowing to the world's standards. Let us all be humble Shadrachs,
Meshachs, and Abednegos who see the lines clearly, follow God fearlessly,
gain for Him the glory and raise a standard for the church of tomorrow. Each
of us must respond; what will your response be?
JUST A THOUGHT
The faith that throws itself entirely upon God with no
possible turning back will not be disappointed.
LESSON 4
PROPHECIES ABOUT CHRIST
Scripture Texts: Isaiah 7:14; Matthew 1:18-23; Isaiah 53:1-3; John 12:37-
Prophecies concerning Christ and His visit to the earth form a very impor-
tant part of Bible history. Today, we study three sets of Scriptures giving
prophecies and their fulfillment.
The Old Testament writings studied today were written several hundred
years before Christ's birth. One writer wrote, and another writer, hundreds
of years later, recorded its fulfillment. Not one prophecy failed; all were ful-
filled. Often the New Testament says, "That it might be fulfilled."
For these many and detailed prophecies to come true after several hundred
years means God was speaking. This proves the Bible is true, that the writers
were inspired by God, told by Him what to write.
MEMORY VERSE: But those things, which God before had shewed by the
mouth of all his prophets, that Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled.
—Acts 3:18
The Sign of Immanuel
Isaiah 7:14 The Lord himself shall give you a sign. This was God's
plan, and He would carry it out. A virgin shall conceive, and bear a son.
This would be a miracle, a thing impossible with man. God is not confined
or limited by the laws of nature; He established nature's laws. This prophecy
was spoken by Isaiah to wicked King Ahaz somewhere around 740 B.C.
Matthew 1:18 When ... Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they
came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost. This proves
without a doubt that Joseph was not the father of Jesus. He and Mary were
engaged but not yet married. Mary was a virgin.
Matthew 1:22-23 This was done, that it might be fulfilled which was
spoken ... by the prophet—not one word of God will be allowed to fail. The
birth of Jesus was definitely the event to which this prediction pointed.
Man's Attitude Foreseen
Isaiah 53:1-3 Who hath believed? It does not seem possible that when
the Creator visited His earth so few would believe Him and that He would be
despised and rejected of men. Yet, around 730 years after this prophecy
was made, the following is recorded in God's Word.
John 12:37-38 They believed not on him. The people's unbelief fulfilled
this prophecy of Isaiah. Does the fact that God knew beforehand of the
people's sin cause them to sin? No, they did not do it because it was written,
but it was written because they would do it. This does not mean that He
wanted it to be so. He just knew they would choose to do so.
Good Tidings of Salvation
Isaiah 61:1-3 The Spirit of the Lord G OD is upon me ... to preach
good tidings ... to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty ... to
comfort ... to give unto them beauty for ashes. Christ brought these things
to mankind. What a marvelous ministry!
Luke 4:16-17 And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought
up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue. He regularly at-
tended the synagogue, a good example indeed. He stood up for to read ...
the book of the prophet Esaias—the prophecy we just looked at.
Luke 4:21-22 This day is this scripture fulfilled. (Jesus said He was the
One beginning that ministry.) God told Isaiah about it around 730 years be-
fore. The people who saw and heard Jesus that day, who knew Him from ba-
byhood, felt the truth of His claim. They bare him witness, and wondered
at the gracious words. Truly, "in him was life; and the life was the light of
men" (John 1:4).
All Fulfilled
Acts 3:18 Those things, which God before had shewed by the ...
prophets, that Christ should suffer, he hath so fulfilled. Not one word of
God shall fail. It never has. Great is His faithfulness!
Of what practical value are these facts to you and me? They are all-
important. Our eternal salvation rests upon the dependability of God and our
faith in that dependability. "He that cometh to God must believe that he is,
and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him" (Hebrews 11:6).
The proofs established by these prophecies give us a sure ground for faith.
"Seek ye out of the book of the L ORD , and read: no one of these shall fail,
none shall want her mate: for my mouth it hath commanded" (Isaiah 34:16).
Friend, what God commands comes true. Step out on His promises. Jesus
Christ is who the Bible says He is—the Son of God. He is eternal. He is
life—thus, the only source of everlasting life.
Many Prophecies
A few predictive prophecies about Christ you may like to examine are:
Psalm 69:21—Matthew 27:34
Isaiah 9:6-7—Luke 1:30-33
Isaiah 53:5—Matthew 8:16-17
Isaiah 53:7—Luke 23:9
Isaiah 53:12—Mark 15:27-28
Micah 5:2—Matthew 2:1-6
Zechariah 9:9—Matthew 21:1-11
Zechariah 11:12-13—Matthew 26:14-15; 27:3-7; Numbers 9:12; Psalm 34:20
Zechariah 12:10—John 19:33-37

One of the worst dangers that confront the younger
generation is the example set by the
older generation.
LESSON 5
THE BIRTH OF JESUS FORETOLD
Scripture Texts: Luke 1:26-38; Matthew 1:18-21
God had predicted this event over and over. Now the time had come. The
announcement was simple, without fanfare, and not made public, but only to
the two people most concerned. Joseph and Mary lived in Nazareth, a coun-
try village of great natural beauty, but great wickedness as well. The ques-
tion was asked, "Can there any good thing come out of Nazareth?" (John
1:46). Yes, but first He came into Nazareth from God above.
MEMORY VERSE: And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his
name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.
—Matthew 1:21
Mary, Only a Part of God's Plan
Luke 1:26-27 In the sixth month–the sixth month of Elisabeth's preg-
nancy—Gabriel was sent—the same angel who about 530 years before had
spoken to Daniel (Daniel 9:21). Gabriel also spoke to Zacharias (Luke 1:19).
To a virgin—a maiden, never married but engaged to Joseph (Isaiah 7:14).
Luke 1:28-31 Highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed .... No
greater words of encouragement can anyone hear than this priceless greeting.
Troubled ... and cast in her mind—sought an explanation. Gabriel called
Mary highly favoured and blessed. She did not gain this favor through any-
thing she had done. God's favor is not won by our efforts but by trusting in
Him, loving Him, yielding to Him, and by the freedom we allow His life to
have within us. Mary had found God's favor. She was a tool suited to God's
use, a receiver of blessings, not the source of them. In her praise, she
acknowledged her humanity and sin by calling God her Savior (verse 47).
Any inventions of men attempting to lift Mary out of her true position as
purely human like all women only distort the truth, wrongs Mary, and
blasphemes God, whose place is usurped. Mary was only a vessel of clay
used by God for His purpose. Fear not—words used often by angels and by
Jesus. God is gentle and kind. Tormenting fear is not His plan for His people.
Found favour with God—consoling words. Thou shalt conceive ... son ...
JESUS. A name divinely given that would fit His character and mission. He
was to be the Savior.
Luke 1:32-33 Great ... Son of the Highest. The Highest is God Himself.
Throne of his father David. King David was an ancestor of Jesus. Mary
descended from David (as did also Joseph; Luke 2:4). "Of the increase of his
government ... [His kingdom] there shall be no end, upon the throne of
David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment
and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the L ORD of hosts
will perform this" (Isaiah 9:7). He promised David this King would be "of
the fruit of thy body"—that is, David's descendant (Psalm 132:11; 89:3-4).
How Can It Be?
Luke 1:34-38 Said Mary ... How shall this be? She knew the natural
impossibility. This had never happened before and would never happen
again. Know not a man. She stated her virginity. The angel explains, The
Holy Ghost shall come upon thee ... therefore ... called the Son of God.
Called so because He was. He was not born illegitimately. God was His
Father. For with God nothing shall be impossible. Here is the foundation
for all miracles. As the angel spoke, Mary took hold of this truth and re-
sponded favorably. Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me ac-
cording to thy word. Willing and glad to do God's will, she accepted the re-
sponsibility, care, and misunderstanding that would come to her along with
the honor.
Joseph Was Also Part of God's Plan
Matthew 1:18-19 Now we look from Joseph's standpoint. Before they
came together, she was found .... They were not yet married. Betrothal in
those days was practically equivalent to marriage. An engagement could only
be broken through the process of divorce. After the betrothal, the bride lived
with her parents for one year, at the end of which time the marriage cere-
mony was performed. Joseph ... was minded to put her away privily—to
break the engagement without publicity. The discovery was a blow to Joseph,
for he was a righteous man, loving and merciful as well as just. He was being
called on for more kindness than the circumstances seemed to require—for
it would appear Mary had been unfaithful, sinful. His suspicions were what
any man's suspicions would have been. He could have denounced Mary for
infidelity, and her punishment would have been severe. Instead, he chose the
more merciful course and decided to put her away privily, which meant to
give her the bill of divorcement, which the Mosaic Law required. In so doing,
he would have assumed the chief blame for what appeared a scandalous state
of affairs.
Matthew 1:20 Angel of the L ORD appeared ... fear not ... is of the
Holy Ghost. As he dreamed, the angel appeared with a great revelation, cor-
recting his mistake. The coming Baby was of the Holy Ghost. If anyone
finds it hard to believe in the doctrine of the Virgin Birth today, consider that
no one else in all history has found it so hard to believe as did Joseph. Mary's
assurances were of no avail; Joseph had to be assured of this great truth by
revelation from God.
Jesus Christ is the world's greatest miracle. It is fitting that His entrance
into human life should be accompanied by a miracle. For Christ to come
from Heaven to Earth had to be a miracle, no matter how God chose to send
Him. Both the Old Testament and the New Testament begin with a great
miracle. The Old Testament begins by telling us that the Spirit of God moved
upon the face of the waters, and Creation resulted. At the very beginning of
the New Testament is recorded the work of the Holy Spirit, which caused a
new Being to appear among men, a new age in human history to have its
origin.
Matthew 1:21 He shall save his people from their sins. This Son is the
promised One, who was to turn away evil and bring righteousness and great
salvation, He of whom it would be said, "in him was life; and the life was the
light of men" (John 1:4). This birth was the only one of its kind. Right at the
beginning of the Gospel, we are informed of the fact that Jesus Christ is the
Savior from sin. He is much more than a leader, teacher, or great person.
What is He to you?
JUST A THOUGHT
Serving my own comfort or pleasure is not serving God.
LESSON 6
CHRIST—THE KING—IS BORN
Scripture Text: Luke 2:1-18
Jesus was not just a great person who happened to appear in the course
of history. His coming was designed by God and foretold by the prophets.
The coming of Jesus Christ was according to prophecy. The angel assured
Joseph as to the nature of the babe, and then without hesitation, Joseph mar-
ried Mary. Joseph's faith and quick compliance with the divine command are
impressive. The unusual announcement in last week's lesson becomes an un-
usual fulfillment in today's study. The birth of Jesus was the greatest event
that ever happened on this earth.
MEMORY VERSE: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and
we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of
grace and truth.
—John 1:14
The Taxing
Luke 2:1-5 Caesar Augustus—Palestine was under the rule of Rome
with Caesar as the emperor. The Roman Empire was vast, and the resentful
nations were held in check by fear of Caesar. He was an absolute monarch,
but his private life was a stench in the minds of all decent people. At this
time, the Prince of Peace was born, and His ideals, programs, and promises
were entirely different from those of Augustus. All the world should be
taxed—all the Roman Empire. All went to be taxed—Rome ruled the entire
then-known world. Caesar called for an enrollment (a census) and decreed
that no one could be enrolled by proxy. Mary, in her delicate condition,
traveled with Joseph ... out of ... Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of
David—from the north to the south over seventy-five miles.
Which is called Bethlehem ... he was of the house and lineage of Da-
vid. (See genealogies in Matthew 1:1-17.) Bethlehem means "house of
bread." Here, the Bread of Life would be born. Joseph was of the house and
family of David; so was Mary. Although He came with no aspiration of be-
ing an earthly king, Christ had the bloodline of a king. The Jewish nation was
looking for the coming of the Messiah, a ruler, a new king (Isaiah 9:6-7).
Jesus was a descendant of David on His human side. The finger of God
had touched His mother, and she had conceived under the power of the Holy
Spirit. He was God-Man, and only such a Being could be the world's Savior.
God had to bring something down from the far reaches of Heaven to redeem
us from sin's power. This was so much more than any earthly king could ac-
complish.
No Room in the Inn
Luke 2:6-7 And so it was—God knew it would be so and told Micah to
write it over seven hundred years earlier (Micah 5:2). Brought forth her
firstborn son—no fanfare, just a simple record of the entrance of the great
Creator into this world. Swaddling clothes ... a manger ... no room for
them in the inn. The word inn means "guest chamber or lodging place."
There was no room for Jesus that night "in the inn," and there has been
no room for Him in the hearts of men ever since. Many still turn Him away
because they do not want to be disturbed in their sleep. They do not wish for
Him to interfere with their lives. The Jewish people wanted a king who could
unseat Augustus, the self-centered tyrant, and bring peace to their earthly
kingdom. Against this man of worldly power, God held up a little Baby.
Good Tidings
Luke 2:8-11 Shepherds abiding in the field—lowly, common workers.
Angel of the Lord came upon them—the revelation took place in the quiet
of the open fields. Often, God makes His greatest revelations not in the earth-
quake or the fire or the roaring tempest, but in the still, small voice. God's
message was sent to a lowly people—shepherds. The One whose birth was
announced was to be the Good Shepherd (John 10:11). The shepherds were
watching over flocks of sheep that were to be used in the Temple sacrifice.
This night they heard the announcement of the birth of One who was to be
"the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world" (John 1:29). The
revelation of history's greatest event was made to a group of humble people.
The glory of the Lord still shines round about the openhearted.
Fear not—God does not wish to frighten. We can almost see His out-
stretched arms in the message of good tidings of great joy ... to all peo-
ple—the message of salvation. Unto you ... a Saviour ... Christ the Lord.
He gave the gift the world most needed. He came to all of us. Here was the
Prophet, Priest, and King promised by God in the prophecies. He is Master
and Ruler. Here we see the spiritual King set against an earthly tyrant.
This contrast comes down to today and into our own lives, where worldli-
ness and spirituality are in deadly conflict. In today's lesson, we see the
heavenly King who was born into the world so thoroughly disguised by
humanity and by the disregard of men that few understood His nature except
a little group of shepherds. That a Savior was born is not enough; we must
seek and find Him personally through divine revelation.
Luke 2:12-14 Suddenly ... a multitude of the heavenly host—it took
only one angel to deliver the message, but all Heaven in overflowing joy
joined in the praise. Glory to God—to Him alone the glory belongs. It was
His plan and doing. On earth peace—Jesus did not bring or promise peace
among the nations, but He brought soul peace—individual peace (John
14:27). Good will—the goodwill of Heaven being shown to the needy ones
of earth. Thank God for His love and goodness!
Their Response
Luke 2:15-18 Let us now go ... and see—no question, just simple faith.
They came ... and found—just as the angel had spoken. Had seen it, they
made known abroad—the normal response is to tell the good news of Jesus
to every human soul. This first Gospel sermon had three points: (1) do not
be afraid; (2) be filled with joy; and (3) "unto you is born ... a Saviour"
(Luke 2:11). That is the Gospel—old and yet ever new. Only faith in Christ
can dispel fear. Joy does not come through the possession of anything but
God's great gift. Joy is God's gift, and it may be the possession of anyone
who is willing to believe and accept.
There are many things that crowd Christ out, such as modern political, in-
tellectual, and social life. Is He crowded out of your heart? If so, why?
JUST A THOUGHT
The heart of the world is already filled with other things.
LESSON 7
THE BOYHOOD AND YOUTH OF JESUS
Scripture Text: Luke 2:40-52
Luke, as a companion of Paul, had the opportunity to come in contact
with many of the people who had a prominent part in the Lord's ministry. As
a competent historian and true man of God, he wrote, under God's guidance,
the only account of the early years of the life of Christ. Twelve years have
passed since the time of our last lesson. In this lesson, we look at the one
view written of Jesus as a child, a boy of twelve. Jesus came to do, above all
other things, the will of His Father, God. This governed all His life. We find
in today's lesson, the lesser must give way to the greater. We see Christ at
the beginning of His divine authority and mission, that of being about His
Father's business.
MEMORY VERSE: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus
is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through
his name.
—John 20:31
Jesus Was a Normal Human Child
Luke 2:40 The best homes in every generation are those that cherish
Christian ideals and put responsibility on the growing children. In this home,
the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit ... wisdom ... the grace of God
was upon him. Physically, mentally, spiritually, He developed as any child
should, no doubt in the highest degree. God's grace rested on Him. God could
have sent the Savior as a mature man, but He chose to allow Him to grow up
as all other humans do, to pass through the different stages of development,
and thus reveal to future generations the capabilities of human nature at its
best. Jesus was a great example in handling the trials and problems of grow-
ing up through the uncertain years of youth. Pictures of Jesus that present
Him as physically weak find no confirmation in the Word of God. He grew
physically and was also full of wisdom. He grew mentally like every other
normal child. And the grace of God was upon Him as it rests upon all chil-
dren, but its application to His life depended upon Mary and Joseph. Today,
many parents who neglect salvation and live a careless or wicked life keep
the grace of God from operating to their child's benefit.
The Boy in the Temple
Luke 2:41-47 Went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the pass-
over—our Lord was brought up in a home where parents set a good example
for their children by faithfully attending to their duties of worship. They went
regularly every year. Twelve years old—the age when a Hebrew boy became
responsible to the Law. As they returned, the child Jesus tarried behind
... Joseph and his mother knew not of it. We must make certain Jesus is
with us before we start out anywhere. They, supposing him to have been
in the company.... Here is a mistake so common to us today; we suppose
Christ is with us, in our lives, without checking carefully to be sure. Went
a day's journey ... sought him among their kinfolk and acquaintance.
Found him not. Jesus cannot be found among worldly friends and relations.
Turned back—a wise decision. After three days—they had lost Jesus in one
day, but it required three days to find Him. It always takes more time to find
Christ after we have left Him than the short time it takes to lose Him. Found
him in the temple—after looking everywhere else, they found Him in the
natural place to look for Christ. Astonished at his understanding and
answers. Here He was putting to use the "spirit," "wisdom," and "the grace
of God" spoken of in verse 40.
The Father's Business
Luke 2:48-50 Amazed—at the unusual situation of Jesus questioning and
answering the great religious minds of that day. It is important to realize
there is greatness in today's children, and the great issues of tomorrow will
be dealt with by those who today are immature. Mary and Joseph had not
sought Jesus in the Temple first. They may have thought Jesus, as other boys
His age, had become interested in the excitement of the big city. Although,
He was a normal boy, Jesus was also the most extraordinary Person ever
born on the earth. His parents had taught Him to put God and worship first,
yet, they seemingly did not expect Him to do so at such an early age. How
is it ...? Jesus, from His viewpoint of carrying forward Heaven's purposes,
set values in their proper places.
Wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business? Jesus was con-
cerned with the things of His Heavenly Father and His business. These words
must have reminded Mary of the words spoken by the angel twelve years
before. Joseph knew that he was not Jesus' father. His business was that of
a carpenter, and the young Jesus learned responsibility while helping make
plows and yokes. This was not the business Jesus was speaking of. Jesus had
a sense of mission, a knowledge of the purpose for which He was born.
Children need to be taught this today. Jesus' actions were with a purpose,
seeing the goal clearly ahead. That goal He stated was my Father's busi-
ness. What He had just done furthered that business. Here was Jesus at the
very beginning of His spiritual work saying He intended to put God first and
keep Him there. Nothing would come before the Father and His business.
Something great was happening. The child was outgrowing His parents. May
it ever be true with our children. They understood not the saying. It was
greater than human wisdom.
Jesus Was Obedient
Luke 2:51-52 Went down with them ... was subject unto them—in
keeping with the whole plan of His stooping to become human, Jesus obeyed
His parents as every human child should. Mary kept all these sayings in her
heart.
Youth is invariably a period of turmoil and struggle. A young man must
wrestle with his passions, think through his problems, see what he wants to
make out of his life, rise above his frustrations, and resolve his inner con-
flicts. Jesus increased in wisdom—in knowledge and the capacity to use
that knowledge to great advantage. He increased in stature. Again we see the
strong Jesus, setting at naught the weak figure whom artists have often mis-
takenly created. He increased in favour with God and man. He became a
servant of both—a servant of God and a servant of men under God. God
loved Him for His perfect obedience; men loved Him for His faithfulness and
His willingness to be helpful. Mary and Joseph gave every generation a good
example of parenthood. Their home was a fit place for the training of the
Lord Jesus, who became the Savior of the world. He is the Source of
Life—everlasting Life.
JUST A THOUGHT
When it can be said of anyone that he has the favor of
God and men, that person has attained the
ultimate in distinction.
LESSON 8
CHRIST—BAPTIZED AND TEMPTED
Scripture Texts: Matthew 3:13-17; 4:1-11
This lesson discusses Jesus' baptism and temptations and relates His vic-
tory over these temptations to situations we face today. Of the eighteen years
since the events of our last lesson, God is silent. He who had been a village
carpenter became a man of destiny. Let us try to put ourselves in His place
and see if we can understand the problems He encountered. Two important
events followed His baptism: (1) God witnessed that His Spirit was on
Christ, and (2) God approved Him as His Son. Because of this, the people
had no reason to reject Him or His teachings.
MEMORY VERSE: For in that he himself hath suffered being tempted, he
is able to succour them that are tempted.
—Hebrews 2:18
The Heavens Opened
Matthew 3:13-17 Then cometh Jesus ... unto John, to be baptized
(immersed). John forbad ... I have need—John knew he was inferior to Je-
sus. Suffer it ... now ... it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness. Jesus' life
was to lack nothing. He is our perfect example in all things. Jesus ... went
up straightway out of the water—He had been immersed. Heavens were
opened—so that the people who were on hand could see and understand the
message was from God. The Spirit of God descending—the Spirit of God
already dwelt in Christ, but God wanted everyone to know Christ was be-
ginning the work He was sent to do. Descending like a dove—here, the
symbol of peace rested on the Prince of Peace.
When Jesus came up out of the water ... the heavens were opened ... the
Spirit of God ... lighting upon him ... a voice from heaven, saying, This
is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased—testified of His divine
Sonship and the perfection of His life. The Jews charged Christ with
blasphemy when He claimed to be God's Son. God had verified this truth,
proving them wrong. This was the voice of God, clearly heard by all who
were there. What happened to Christ symbolizes what always happens to the
consecrated heart. When we renounce sin and declare to the world our
intention to do God's will, the Heavens will open and the Spirit will descend
on our souls.
Temptation Follows Exaltation
Matthew 4:1-3 Led up of the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted
of the devil—a planned combat. Jesus knew the purpose of His coming was
to do the will of God. Now He was to receive exact instruction and be pre-
paration for His mission to the world. Here we find the power of evil directed
against that spotless life to destroy it and render it useless to the world's
spiritual needs. Why did God not shield His Son from this agonizing experi-
ence that might indeed have destroyed His usefulness before He began? Char-
acter grows through testing. Jesus had to be tempted in all the ways that hu-
man nature is subject to temptation. It was part of the price He had to pay
in order to be our example in all things (Hebrews 2:18; 4:15).
Here are two precious truths that will help us in temptation: (1) our Lord
was tempted; thus, we can expect to be also; and (2) throughout His
temptation, Jesus was in the power of the Spirit. The first Adam met temp-
tation and yielded. He made the mistake of feeling he could better guide his
own life. The second Adam met temptation and resisted. To Him, there was
no life worth living apart from yielding to the will of God. Because Jesus met
and conquered the foe, He is able to succor us. We often seem to think that
surrendering our lives to God will eliminate all our struggles. Yet, in many
instances, the opposite is true. The tempter came to him—Christ had been
exalted by the Father; now He was to be tempted. It is good to remember that
when we are high in the Spirit, the devil is waiting to spoil it all by tempting
us in some way. If thou be the Son of God—he made the issue to be
whether Jesus was the Son of God—a deceitful trick. Christ had been forty
days without natural food. Through God's miraculous power, the processes
of nature were temporarily changed in some way. But at the end of forty
days, a physical hunger of a great nature swept over this very human Jesus.
Command that these stones be made bread—an appeal to Jesus' desire for
food. This was the same tool Satan used in the garden.
Not By Bread Alone
Matthew 4:4 He answered ... It is written—Jesus appealed to the au-
thority of God's Word (Deuteronomy 8:3). Man shall not live by bread
alone—Jesus thought of the much greater importance of spiritual life than
physical. He did not need to trouble His mind about physical needs. God put
Him there, and God would take care of Him. But by every word ... out of
the mouth of God—God's Word sustains life. The bread theory is prevalent
in modern life by politicians and leaders in education. The theory is that if
you give men all they need to be well-fed and comfortable, their lives will be
rich. The bread theory is based on materialism—that man can live by bread
alone. It is deception that only leads the world into further dissatisfaction
(Matthew 6:25).
Matthew 4:5-7 Devil taketh him up—not literally, but in His mind—in-
to the holy city—Jerusalem—pinnacle of the temple .... If thou be the
Son—as before, a challenge to prove it—cast thyself down: for it is writ-
ten. Now Satan quoted Scripture (Psalm 91:11-12). Having failed with the
bread theory, Satan brought his power theory before Jesus. This evil theory
is based on compromise. Satan was suggesting Jesus avoid the Cross and
take the easy route to world conquest. Christ did not come to conquer the
world but to save it. He needed no forced proof, for God had spoken it (John
10:25). Jesus said ... it is written .... Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy
God (Deuteronomy 6:16). It is written is our greatest defense against the de-
ceiving powers of Satan today.
Get Thee Hence
Matthew 4:8-11 Again—the devil is persistent—taketh him up—again,
in His mind —into ... high mountain ... sheweth ... kingdoms ... glory ...
All these things will I give thee, if—a small price? Satan required the com-
plete surrender of Himself, His position, authority, purpose, and future—the
loss of all Jesus came to accomplish. In so doing, He would no longer have
had that "life" to give, which is "the light of men" (John 1:4). Having failed
in presenting the bread theory and the power theory, Satan then presented the
main aim he desired—what he would give Jesus if thou wilt ... worship me.
This evil philosophy is based on control by man rule. The trouble with all
Satan's suggestions, both then and now, is that they leave God out of the
picture.
Satan worked through Christ's mind, just as he works through ours. There
was no literal mountain where Christ was taken, and Satan had no kingdom
to give then, as he has none now. It was just talk. Then saith Jesus ... Get
thee hence, Satan—a complete separation, no compromise. It was the only
way for Jesus then; it is the only way for us now (James 4:7).
It is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord ... and him only. Worship
of God allows no sharing with another (Deuteronomy 8:19). Devil
leaveth—when the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from
Him for a season. Angels ... ministered—the decision was all for Christ to
make, but when it was made, the Father sent help and comfort (both spiritual
and physical). Resist the devil, decide for the Lord, and you will be surprised
at the sudden abundance of strength and peace that is yours. Continue to
resist in the power of the Spirit, and you will have continuous victory. If the
Son needed the Spirit, how much more do we?
JUST A THOUGHT
Satan tempts us as he tempted our Lord, and when he leaves
us, keep in mind he will return again.
LESSON 9
CHRIST PREACHED A NEW MESSAGE
Scripture Text: Matthew 5:1-12
Today's lesson, commonly spoken of as the Sermon on the Mount, deals
with the new law of Christian living each disciple of Christ must attain in or-
der to live a life acceptable to God. Christ brought forth this new teaching
that constituted the new standard of life in contrast with the Mosaic Law.
This lesson discusses the meaning of the Beatitudes to show how the teach-
ings expressed in them can enrich our lives. The study of the Beatitudes is
the way to discover what the Christian life involves—its obligations, respon-
sibilities, and rewards.
MEMORY VERSE: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see
your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
—Matthew 5:16
Blessedness
The Beatitudes are the first part of what is known as the Sermon on the
Mount. In Matthew's Gospel, the sermon runs from the first verse of the fifth
chapter to the end of the seventh chapter. The sermon is a series of teachings
given by Jesus to His followers so that they might know clearly what was
required of them. He asked for perfection and required a righteousness that
went beyond the Ten Commandments.
A person can be blessed and yet not happy, and a person can be happy
and not blessed. Blessedness is what we call "soul peace." It is inner content-
ment, spiritual rest, and the joy that comes from knowing God is our Father,
and He is mighty to save. In these verses, Jesus defined the sort of people He
would call blessed. The Ten Commandments are characteristic of the Old
Testament, the Beatitudes of the New Testament. Moses received the Com-
mandments on Mount Sinai; Jesus preached the new commandments on, it is
assumed, the Mount of Olives.
The Commandments are mainly negative—Thou shalt not; Jesus said,
"Blessed are ...." The Commandments are demands; the Beatitudes are invita-
tions to a worship of love.
The Beatitudes
Matthew 5:1-3 Seeing the multitudes, he went up into a mountain.
Jesus taught, preached, and healed throughout Galilee. As a result of the
wide fame this gave Him, large crowds gathered. Blessed are the poor in
spirit. These are people who do not depend upon their own riches and pos-
sessions, but who fully depend upon God. They recognize that they need
something within, which nothing on the outside can produce (2 Corinthians
6:10). This message went forth with force and conviction. The people knew
that Jesus knew what He was talking about and practiced what He preached.
Theirs is the kingdom. Only those who are conscious of their own insuf-
ficiency and inadequacy are fit to enter God's kingdom.
Matthew 5:4 Blessed are they that mourn—not sad-faced, gloomy kill-
joys, the true mourners are those who are sensitive to their own sin and
unworthiness and to the sins and miseries of a lost world. They mourn be-
cause evil seems so strong and they are weak. The mourners are like the
psalmist in Psalm 137:4. They mourn because they see their need of God and
that many of their fellowmen are heading for eternity in a lost condition.
They shall be comforted—by God through His forgiveness, mercy, and
victory He gives over all sin and evil.
Matthew 5:5 Blessed are the meek—not the timid, subdued, browbeaten
souls. The meek are humble, those who do not push and shove to get ahead,
but who are patient and content. They are gentle with others. The heart of the
meek submits to God's will and faithfully obeys God's Word. Christ Himself
gave the best definition of the word meek in Matthew 11:29. The world seeks
money, pleasure, and position. Jesus did not say that the rich in this world's
goods are blessed, but He said that the meek are blessed. They will obtain the
highest position and possession. They shall inherit the earth—they shall
reign over earthly things ("earthen vessels"; 2 Corinthians 4:7); earthly things
will not reign over them.
Matthew 5:6 Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righ-
teousness—a desire from the heart for the soul to be fed the bread of life and
to drink of the water of life, to desire spiritual things more than material
things. Jesus wants no self-satisfied followers who are willing to let well
enough alone. He pronounces a blessing on those who are restlessly seeking
a better world and a better life for themselves and others. Christ blesses those
who desire spiritual advancement. They shall be filled. Those living this way
will be satisfied by the deep joy of living a Spirit-filled life.
Matthew 5:7 Blessed are the merciful—this is basic Christian living
(James 2:13). If we are spiritually alive, we will be merciful. This is far from
the teaching of "eye for eye, tooth for tooth" (Deuteronomy 19:21). In the
Parable of the Unmerciful Servant (Matthew 18:21-35), Jesus told His disci-
ples that they must forgive others to receive God's forgiveness (Mark 11:25).
Only if we are merciful will we obtain mercy. Here, the law of sowing and
reaping comes into this lesson.
Matthew 5:8 Blessed are the pure in heart—this refers to sincerity,
honesty, and a single, undivided loyalty to God. We have the assurance of
God's presence in our lives and a true fellowship with Him in His kingdom
in this present time. With this experience in a sinless heart, we shall see
God. A heart with sin cannot be pure. Heart purity results in an outward
change as well.
Matthew 5:9 Blessed are the peacemakers—makers of peace. How des-
perately the world needs them today! We all want peace—but how few there
are who work for peace. The peacemakers are those who overcome evil with
good, who go out of their way to reconcile enemies. They shall be called the
children of God. With the Prince of Peace, you can be a peacemaker.
Matthew 5:10-12 Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteous-
ness' sake. Followers of Christ must remain true even when they suffer hate
and injustice. They must accept mistreatment for their loyalty to God. Those
who take the Christian faith seriously soon find they are at odds with many
people, programs, and policies of the world (2 Timothy 3:12). They might be
shunned by their former friends, lied about, and taunted by all those who love
the darkness and hate the light. The reward is great—great is your reward
in heaven.
JUST A THOUGHT
To be a Christian is to follow the Leader whose steps led to
rejection, humiliation, and death on the Cross.
LESSON 10
SOME OF CHRIST'S EARLY MIRACLES
Scripture Text: Matthew 8:1-4, 14-17, 23-27
Do not confuse a miracle with magic. Miracles require a special manifes-
tation of God's power. Magic is either imaginary or done through the use of
natural laws available to all to produce mystifying results that anyone could
do by the same methods. Sometimes, what is considered magic is a supernat-
ural work of the devil; there are Biblical examples.
This lesson reveals something of the life in Jesus and of His power over
physical disease and death. His life has just as much power over spiritual
death. We can have this spiritual life.
MEMORY VERSE: Jesus answered them, I told you, and ye believed not:
the works that I do in my Father's name, they bear witness of me.
—John 10:25
Life Conquers Death
Matthew 8:1-4 When he was come down from the mountain—from
preaching the Sermon on the Mount. There came a leper and worshipped
him—he believed Jesus was God and worthy of worship. He opened his heart
to Jesus. If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean—no question about Jesus'
power to heal, but the leper was not sure it was His will. Jesus ... touched
him ... I will; be thou clean. Jesus stretched out His hand to this diseased
man whom all others avoided. The condition of a man's body makes no dif-
ference to Him; what matters is the condition of his heart. God loves the
whole world, but salvation is a process of singling out the individual who
feels his need and cries out to God. Look at this wretched man—what a fear-
ful sight! Leprosy represents as a type of sin unto death, a slow decay to
which man could give no cure. The touching of the leper by Jesus has double
significance: the leper comes in faith expecting Jesus to touch him, while the
ever-present critics watch, believing that He will not dare. Jesus defies the
onlookers, breaks through the Levitical Law, heals the leper, and, in so do-
ing, establishes the higher law of love.
Leprosy works as cruelly on a man's spirit as on his body. In answer to
faith, the touch of Christ restores the spirit and heals the body's decay. This
miracle proves God cares for both the spiritual and physical well-being of the
individual. The story of the leper teaches that no man is so diseased, filthy,
forsaken, or beaten down by society, but that Christ's touch can heal and
make him clean. Christ's atonement provided for both the soul and body of
mankind, showing Jesus is concerned for both.
Miracles, Not Magic
Matthew 8:14-15 Peter's ... wife's mother ... sick of a fever. Peter's
mother-in-law had a physical need. He touched her hand—just a
touch—fever left her ... she arose ... ministered—another miracle. This
was not magic, but the divine power of God. The Bible is so full of miracles
that to discard miracles is to discard the Bible.
Matthew 8:16-17 They brought unto him many ... possessed with
devils—spirits of demons dwelt in the bodies of these people, controlling
them. There are also devil-possessed people today. Here, we witness a spir-
itual sickness. He cast out the spirits with his word. God at Creation
spoke, and things came into existence by the power of His Word. By that
same Word, Christ spoke and demons departed. There is but one power over
Satan—the power of God's Word (Hebrews 4:12). These were done that it
might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias. (Compare with Isaiah 53:4-
5). It is clear that destroying the power of Satan and healing the body were
part of Christ's work of which Isaiah wrote some seven hundred years before.
Christ came to heal bodies as well as to take away sins.
The Storm Stilled
Matthew 8:23-24 Entered into a ship ... great tempest ... ship was cov-
ered with the waves: but he was asleep. Picture the scene—the ship cross-
ing Galilee in a great storm, terrified disciples, and the tired, sleeping Jesus.
Matthew 8:25-26 Disciples ... awoke him, saying, Lord, save us: we
perish. They had witnessed things over and over again that made them know
He had power over every situation. Why are ye fearful, O ye of little faith?
Sufficient faith would have driven out the fear. Here was Jesus with them;
they were all in the same boat; nothing would happen to them that would not
happen to Jesus. Proper faith in Christ brings a deep-settled peace through
the storms we face in this sea of life.
He ... rebuked the winds and the sea; and there was a great calm.
Before salvation, we were all tossed about on the sea of life by the mighty
waves of sin, but when we called on Jesus, He spoke the Word and calmed
the troubled waters of our souls. Although there will be times when our ships
will sail through rough waters, if Christ is on board, He will take us safely
through by His Word.
Be Thankful
Matthew 8:27 But the men marvelled—oh, that men would marvel more
and thank God for His faithfulness in stilling life's storms for us! We take too
much for granted. What manner of man ... even the winds and the sea
obey him! Only One is Master of the winds and seas, the One who made
them.
One more miracle to confirm in the minds of men in all generations is the
truth that this Jesus is the Son of God. Words are effective to a degree, but
works are more convincing. People hear about the power of God, but what
they really want and need is to see a manifestation of the power of Christ.
God's miracle power has never been withdrawn or limited. Many can testify
to present-day miracles. "All things are possible to him that believeth" (Mark
JUST A THOUGHT
The whole world is a series of miracles,
but we are so used to them,
we call them ordinary things.
LESSON 11
CHRIST AUTHORIZED APOSTLES
Scripture Text: Matthew 10:1-10, 34-39
When God calls us to His work, He gives power to do that work. When
we choose our own way, we cannot expect His help. Uncalled ones are unem-
powered ones. He calls not only leaders but each of us to some place in His
work. If we follow His leading, receive His Spirit, pray, study, and exercise
to develop, He will enable us to fill those places. Jesus promised those He
sent, then, and from that time on, "Lo, I am with you alway" (Matthew
This lesson aims to point out the need for workers to go into all the world
and to set forth the opportunities and difficulties that confront Jesus' follow-
ers in their mission.
MEMORY VERSE: He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth
his life for my sake shall find it.
—Matthew 10:39
Jesus Gave Them Authority
Matthew 10:1 He ... called unto him his twelve disciples. Jesus gave
them authority for a special work. Rome would not have given men like Pe-
ter, Thomas, James, and John authority because they were not men with
clenched fists. Caiaphas would never have given them authority because they
were unlearned men. But Jesus did. They were given authority that men who
seized power and tried to assume authority could not come close to. Gave
them power against unclean spirits. These spirits are demons and have
greater power than humans. No human can withstand them without power
from God. And to heal—neither can a human do this in his own power.
When we operate under divine authority, no unclean spirit or sickness can
stand against the supernatural power of Christ's authority.
Matthew 10:2-7 Names of the twelve—all were common workingmen,
"unlearned and ignorant" (Acts 4:13). Go not into the way of the Gentiles,
and ... Samaritans—a temporary command for the present. Later on, Paul
was to go to the Gentiles (Acts 13:46-47). Go rather to the lost sheep ... of
Israel—this limitation of their efforts was put on them because the time had
not yet come for them to minister to the Gentile nations. It took a marvelous
vision later to convince Peter of the worldwide need of the Gospel. As ye go,
preach. We are to preach every minute of the day, not necessarily by the
spoken word but by conducting ourselves in such a way that people will see
the Gospel of Christ manifested in our lives. Their message was a simple
one: The kingdom of heaven is at hand. Heaven came to earth in the Person
of Jesus. It was He who established the heavenly life among men. By the ex-
ercising of the authority which He has given us, by the consecrating of our
hearts to His Spirit and by continually submitting to His guidance, through
wholehearted service, we can be co-workers with Him in His great kingdom.
At hand—for you, me, and all the world.
Our Working Orders
Matthew 10:8-10 Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast
out devils—the message was backed up and verified by miracles. The sick
were healed, the infected cleansed, the dead raised, and the distraught by
Satan restored to sanity. Both physical and spiritual miracles were auth-
orized. In a sense, it can be said that the business of the church is to bring
Heaven down to earth. Provide neither gold (money), scrip (food), two
coats (clothing), staves (weapons). Did God want them to be foolish? No,
God just had a better way. The workman is worthy of his meat (food). God
was going to care for them through His other children, thus giving a double
blessing to both the giver and the receiver. The Apostles "lacked ... nothing"
(Luke 22:35). (Later Jesus was to tell them to take such things as they
needed; Luke 22:36.) The twelve received two temporary commands applying
to that trip alone—to go to Israel only and carry no provisions. This shows
God's power and will to provide for His servants. It is not wrong but our
duty to use our resources to supply our needs so long as doing so does not
turn our eyes from Jesus or hinder in the work He has given us. Christ wants
our faith placed in Him as Provider. God still provides for those who cut
loose from dependence on self and the world, put God's will first, and trust
Him for all their needs (Matthew 6:33).
The Reward of the Righteous
Matthew 10:34-38 Not ... peace, but a sword. Christ's Gospel is revolu-
tionary. It upsets lives, customs, families, and nations. Make an all-out com-
mitment to Christ, and you will see and feel the sword. Christ's program is
not one of complacency, compromise, or acceptance of everything. It is one
of final separation between right and wrong, true and false, holiness and sin.
You will find there is war between Christ's followers and Satan. Christ's
peace is with God in the heart, not peace with the world. He that loveth
father or mother more than me is not worthy of me—our dearest earthly
loves must be second to our love for Christ. He that taketh not his cross ...
is not worthy of me. The counsel is to be prepared for opposition as we take
our stand for Christ. Let us be neither amazed nor discouraged if men jeer at
us and oppose us when we take our stand for the things of Christ against
their love of comfort, spiritual indifference, and evil ways. Taketh—taking
our cross is a voluntary acceptance of all the hardship and sacrifice that
comes because of our devotion to Him. Our Lord's basic demand is that we
surrender to His will.
Matthew 10:39 Findeth his life shall lose it—accept the cross—the daily
pain and death to self and the flesh. (Read Matthew 16:24-25.) There are
those who live for themselves, who draw to themselves the pleasures, posses-
sions, friends, and accomplishments that they think will build their lives up
into something that will please themselves. Such lives may appear a great
success in this world, but they will be lost in the next one. Loseth his life for
my sake shall find it. He who lives for the Lord, who has died to self and
gives himself, his possessions, labor, love, and life for Jesus' sake, who mea-
sures his actions by whether they will please and serve God, who counts not
his life dear unto himself, will live eternally in Heaven. Not only that, but
this life is worth living in this world as well. When God calls us to His work,
He gives power to do that work. When we try to choose our own way, we
cannot expect His help. Uncalled ones are unempowered ones. He calls not
only leaders but each of us to a place in His work (1 Corinthians 12:18).
JUST A THOUGHT
We are called by Jesus when the Spirit first speaks to our
hearts; we are commissioned when some opportunity
for service challenges us.
LESSON 12
JESUS CLEANSED THE TEMPLE
Scripture Text: John 2:13-17
Following the first miracle that He performed, that of turning water into
wine in Cana of Galilee, Jesus went up to Jerusalem for the Jews' Passover.
This brings us to the study of today's lesson, in which we are shown our
Lord's respect for the house and worship of God. Jesus gives us insight
through these Scriptures of how He expects men and women to conduct
themselves in His house of worship. Today we see a contrast of Christ's
values set up against the values of the world and its worldlings concerning
God's house of worship.
MEMORY VERSE: And said unto them, It is written, My house shall be
called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.
—Matthew 21:13
Christ Was No Religious Rebel
John 2:13 Jews' passover was at hand, and Jesus went up to Jerusa-
lem. Our Lord's rebellion against many persons and practices of His day may
cause us to be blinded to the true purpose of Christ's action. It is sure that
He opposed the established religion. He poured the vials of His criticism up-
on those who held high ecclesiastical offices in His day. This often gives the
impression that Jesus was a rebel against the faith of His people, the Jews.
Jesus was never in rebellion against the revealed religion which had come
down from the days of Moses through the prophets and leaders of the past.
He was in rebellion against the teachings of men who tampered with the true
faith and revised its spiritual position for any sort of personal glory.
Cleansing the Temple
John 2:14 And found in the temple those that sold ... and the changers
... sitting. We see here the attitude of those who carried on business in the
house of God, those who had no interest in true worship but were there for
personal financial gain alone.
People coming to the Passover from a long distance found it more conven-
ient to buy an animal for sacrifice near the Temple than to bring one many
miles. Because the Roman coins of that day bore the image of Caesar, they
could not be used in any temple transaction; so the Roman coin had to be ex-
changed for a Temple coin. At first, booths were set up in the vicinity of the
Temple; then, as time went on, they moved closer and closer to the holy
areas. The high priests could not resist the temptation to grant concessions
to these merchants for a price, and so the moves continued until all the outer
court of the Temple, known as the Court of the Gentiles, was filled with
stalls for sacrificial animals, crates containing doves, and long tables behind
which sat the moneychangers.
The scene was anything but what one would expect to find in the Temple.
Instead of a holy quiet, there was the unholy clamor of merchants selling
their wares. Picture in your mind the bleating of sacrificial animals, the
clinking of coins, the loud laughter, and the dealing of bargainers.
When Jesus saw this, His anger boiled. In this we see the proper use of
anger, a God-given passion. To Christ, the Temple was a holy place, a house
of prayer for all. Changing the holy use of the Temple to a dishonest system
of merchandising caused the pure soul of Jesus to vent the zeal of the Lord.
Zeal is a word derived from a Greek word meaning "to boil."
John 2:15-16 Made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out ...
and overthrew the tables. (Read Malachi 3:1-3.) Make not my Father's
house an house of merchandise. Jesus was angry. He still gets angry when
the house of God is used to carry on personal business. The house of God is
no place to take orders for products you are selling, whether it is Tupperware
or Girl Scout cookies. The child of God should be angry over the materialism
of our day, over the widespread casting aside of holy things in the interest of
comfort and gain.
The scourge of cords needs to be in the hands of every disciple today as
it was in the hands of our Lord. God is still angry concerning things that de-
file His dwelling place. We are "the temple of God" (1 Corinthians 3:16), and
we must drive out anything that would defile the temple of our bodies.
Cleanse Hearts Before Reform
John 2:17 The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up. The house of God
is a place into which non-Jews—unsaved ones—can enter, pray, and hear
from God. Jesus' pattern of reform is to cleanse men's hearts first. He knows
that men's hearts must be made right with God before any real reformation
in conduct can begin.
Jesus' cleansing of the literal Temple is a type of the driving out of all
hindering elements in this living temple of flesh, elements that hinder us from
being fully used for God's designed purpose.
We have here a picture of our Lord's deep spiritual interests in contrast
with the materialism of the priests and Pharisees—the religious men of His
day—and their ignorance of real spiritual worth. Jesus' concern for "the tem-
ple of God" (1 Corinthians 3:17) is His reason for coming as our Savior. He
came to change men's hearts and bring life—eternal life—to dead souls. This
is what causes men to respond with a different attitude when attending the
house of God. It brings respect, reverence, and concern for souls. What is
your attitude toward the house of God?
JUST A THOUGHT
Worship that is missing RESPECT and HUMILITY
is not true worship.
LESSON 13
CHRIST AND NICODEMUS
Scripture Text: John 3:1-12, 16
Today, we take a look at the one Source of true life. It is a fact that a per-
son must be born again to enter the kingdom. Thus, all in the kingdom are
born again. How foolish to call any organization "the church" which includes
those not born again; how futile to try to build a church which includes those
without this experience; how useless to set boundary lines and rules for en-
tering the church when God has already drawn the lines and set up the only
possible rule for entrance! These false lines will finally be swept away, but
while they exist, they confuse and misguide many people.
MEMORY VERSE: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begot-
ten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have ever-
lasting life.
—John 3:16
Visitor by Night
John 3:1-3 Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews. He was a Pharisee, a mem-
ber of the religious group known for its hypocrisy—for devotion to form and
neglect of the spirit. He was a man of authority, superior to others who filled
the Temple. Yet, he showed evidence of sincerity. Came to Jesus by night.
Why he came to Jesus by night, we are not sure. Some teach he was afraid;
others say he desired the privacy of the evening, which provided a better op-
portunity to learn from this great Teacher. Regardless, he sought Jesus. His
associates scorned Jesus and took active steps against His followers (John
9:22; 19:38). Rabbi, we know ... thou art ... from God. He believed in
Christ as far as he had light.
Nicodemus testified for all his group—we know! The miracles had taught
what Jesus intended they should, that the doer of them must have come from
God. Nicodemus addressed Jesus as Rabbi, a title showing great respect.
Seeing the hunger of Nicodemus' heart, Jesus spoke directly to his desire to
enter God's kingdom. Except a man be born again, he cannot .... This is the
only way. No one can have life in Christ without the new birth.
A Strange Doctrine
John 3:4-7 How can a man .... Nicodemus was thinking of the physical
and human power only. Verily, verily—truly, truly—Except a man be born
of water and of the Spirit—the Word and Spirit of God. "The washing of
water by the word" cleanses from "the church" (Ephesians 5:25-26); the
Spirit makes alive (John 6:63; 2 Corinthians 3:6). These do not signify two
steps, but rather two aspects of one operation. The operation (the work) is
rebirth. It includes cleansing and the coming of new life. When that happens,
the person is born again—made a child of God.
That which is born of the flesh is flesh ... born of the Spirit is spirit.
Here we see the separation between earthly, material things and spiritual
things. God's kingdom is spiritual and cannot be entered through a physical
(fleshly) birth but only by the work of the Spirit in the heart. Physical birth,
water baptism, church joining, or any other work or form cannot save or
make our spirits live. Being born of the Spirit can and does.
Jesus told Nicodemus he was on the wrong track. In substance, He said:
"Not external signs but an inner change of heart is what you need, Nicodem-
us." Learning is not enough; there must be life. Nicodemus—a cautious, in-
telligent, and honest man, but only a beginner in the school of God—wanted
more facts, more signs. He desired more of what had already proven inade-
quate. Fact added to fact until the facts become mountain high will not make
one the recipient of God's truth. Jesus declared that what he needed was life.
Men have made flowers, fruit, and many other things that look like the
real thing, but are without that one thing man cannot duplicate—life that God
alone can create. My, what a difference life makes! Christ taught that some-
thing must be added to the natural man to give him eternal life. Life must be
added through a new birth. Nicodemus could not understand this. He pointed
out the impossibility of a physical rebirth. Jesus agreed, but explained that
just as physical birth is needed to bring a body into the world, so spiritual
birth is needed to bring a soul into the kingdom.
In birth, there must be a fertilizing agent. In the case of the body, this
agent is the earthly father; in the case of the soul, it is the Heavenly Father.
The earthly father by his seed begets a son in the flesh; the Heavenly Father
by His Spirit begets a child unto eternal life. Christ came to bring spiritual
life. Everlasting life involves spiritual birth.
All Must Know the Truth
John 3:8-12 The wind ... so is every one ... born of the Spirit—like
wind, it cannot be seen, but it is real. It causes outward effects. But how can
these things be? Nicodemus was a teacher of religion, but he did not under-
stand this truth. Neither can anyone else, except he receives the witness of
the Spirit of Christ. We do not fully understand the wind, but we use it to
sail ships and run windmills. How foolish to refuse to use electricity unless
we fully understood all about it. Unless we ask, as Nicodemus did, why and
how about the deep things of life, we will never receive an explanation. When
we accept what God has offered, the answers will be there. We will begin to
understand. In earthly things we learn and accept. In spiritual things, we ac-
cept and learn.
John 3:16 God so loved ... that he gave ... that whosoever believeth ...
should not perish, but have everlasting life. God gave His Son to save the
world from perishing, but the world did not take the Son of God; We must
believe Jesus Christ is God's Son, that He can and will forgive our sins and
give us life. We must believe enough to repent, let go, and cast ourselves on
the mercy of God to do it. Why does God give so much for nothing? Because
God so loved the world. Whosoever believeth. "Whosoever" takes in all
who will. And as we close this last lesson, let it be with the assurance we can
have eternal life only by believing—believing what we can never by any ex-
ercise of the mind completely understand.
JUST A THOUGHT
We are born as God's CREATURES ;
we are reborn into that spiritual state
that makes us God's SONS and DAUGHTERS .
